sentences.text: Propanoplosaurus was a herbivorous nodosaurid dinosaur found in the Early Cretaceous Patuxent Formation of Maryland, USA.
The preserved length of the specimen is thirteen centimetres, while the total estimated length of the individual was between twenty-four and twenty-eight centimetres.
The fossil specimen is preserved showing the animal lying on its back.
Researchers suggest that osteoderms appearing only on the skull and a long snout with a unique cross-pattern of bone plates were common developmental stages in nodosaurids.
The species Propanoplosaurus marylandicus was named and described by Stanford, Weishampel, and DeLeon in 2011 based on the holotype specimen USNM 540686 found in the Patuxent Formation.
The describers assigned Propanoplosaurus to the family Nodosauridae.
Propanoplosaurus lived during the mid-Cretaceous, specifically the Aptian stage, approximately 112 million years ago in North America, with a time range from 119.57 to 113.2 million years ago.
